title: Determine the sharp net splitting-tax coefficient (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Determine the least net splitting coefficient for 0<t<1. It is finite exactly when sigma>=1; for sigma>1 only two adjacent quotient candidates are needed. The exact family t=1/2, sigma=1+1/(2n) has optimal q=n(n+1); in particular N(1/2,3/2)=8/27. The full completion charge remains paid.

This resolves the net-coefficient question in #6390 and strengthens #4480's bound. Credit #4433/#4832 for the preceding higher-moment framework. Canonical base: 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a. Pending #6390 is pinned at f9e68f40b0da7236a7fad415f7172218c0666d27; all source bytes and other pins are in SOURCES.json.

## Evidence

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/sharp-net-splitting-tax/verify.py
```

Expected: PASS_SHARP_NET_SPLITTING_TAX. Normal/optimized registered and portable replays passed: 16 parameter pairs, 4,608 literal splits, 4,844 separate exact fixtures, 13 semantic controls and eight actual corrupted-package rejections. Two separate mathematical reviews found no unresolved gap.

## Limitations and next questions

No new κ. This is a written universal coefficient theorem with finite corroboration, not a complete native compiler admission. The [companion application](https://github.com/CubeJerry/integer-mult-bounds/blob/223ea940b604c1f8a2bd28093618628ba4a113a4/research/selected6030-smaller-compiler/JOINT-PROOF.md) now supplies a checked selected-source example. Further applications and physical obligations remain open; all five framework assumptions remain. Full-history validation was unavailable in the shallow checkout.
